To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified a novel pathogenic variant c.1508C > G; p.(Glu503*) in HPS1 associated with HPS with fulminant pulmonary fibrosis.
we have described a new variant in HPS1 that leads to fulminant pulmonary fibrosis.
we identified a compound heterozygous variant of HPS gene in a patient with fulminant pulmonary fibrosis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel genetic variant of HHS1 gene in HPS with fulminant progress of pulmonary fibrosis and may be useful in the differential diagnosis of pulmonary fibrosis.
the identification of a novel genetic variant in HPS1 associated with fulminant pulmonary fibrosis.
the clinical and genetic characteristics of a case of pulmonary fibrosis in HPS and the need for early diagnosis and treatment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presented case is the first report of HPS1 compound heterozygosity in the Czech Republic and the first case of HPS1 p.Gln503* variant.
the HPS1 gene is a novel candidate gene for HPS with fulminant pulmonary fibrosis.
this is the first report of a novel genetic variant of HSP1 gene in a patient with HPS and fulminant pulmonary fibrosis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we report a novel compound heterozygosity of HPS1 in a patient with HPS and fulminant progression to pulmonary fibrosis, which was confirmed by genetic testing.
the WES is a useful method for the identification of HPS and other rare diseases.
HPS should be suspected when a patient presents with oculocytaneous albinism and pulmonary fibrosis, even when the patient is older than 40 years of age, as in our case.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HPS is a rare genetic disorder that may present with a wide range of clinical manifestations and that it may be underdiagnosed.
the HPS1 gene should be included in the differential diagnosis of pulmonary fibrosis and the HPS1 genotype may be useful in the prognosis of HPS patients.
the WES approach is a valuable diagnostic tool in the diagnosis of rare genetic diseases.
